problem: Given the curve  $r(t)=8\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+8\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+6t\,k,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=10t,$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$

feedback.problem: Given the curve  $r(t)=⟨2{e}^{t},\,3{e}^{t},\,6{e}^{t}⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=7({e}^{t}-1),$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, since $s=7({e}^{t}-1)$, we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{s}{7} & ={e}^{t}-1 \\ {e}^{t} & =\frac{s}{7}+1 \\ t & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{s+7}{7}).\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{s+7}{7})) \\  & =⟨2{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{s+7}{7})},\,3{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{s+7}{7})},\,6{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{s+7}{7})}⟩ \\  & =⟨2\cdot \frac{s+7}{7},\,3\cdot \frac{s+7}{7},\,6\cdot \frac{s+7}{7}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2s+14}{7},\,\frac{3s+21}{7},\,\frac{6s+42}{7}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{2s+14}{7}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3s+21}{7}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{6s+42}{7})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{7},\,\frac{3}{7},\,\frac{6}{7}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
